exp3: Edit to model_optimized.py immediately followed by 'Record exp3 failure' — reverts the failed optimization and logs it rather than pressing on with a broken variant.
exp4 (max-autotune) after extensive polling times out; agent edits (reverts) then records 'exp4 timeout' — abandons an unproductive direction cleanly.
After exp6, agent does a 'Final confirmation run of exp5' and finalizes exp5 — deliberately selecting the fastest passing implementation instead of keeping the last thing tried.

reasoning: The agent consistently responds to failures by investigating and adjusting: a dtype-targeted TF32-off correction for parity, explicit reverts of failed/timed-out experiments (exp3, exp4), and a final confirmation that reinstates exp5 as the fastest passing variant rather than the last-tried exp6 — clearly satisfying the level-5 anchor (revert bad optimizations, discard non-passing variants) with some level-8 signals (dtype-targeted correction, clean reverts, defensible final selection). It falls short of a full 8/10 because the step index shows no visible systematic root-cause isolation of parity divergence, so I place the observed level at 6.
